title: Bircher oats with stewed Bramley and hazelnuts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, milk, yoghurt, sultanas, orange, apples, honey, hazelnuts and cinnamon are all plain kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, hazelnuts included, is an everyday item at any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a bowl, a small pan and a frying pan are needed, and simmering apples and toasting nuts are beginner techniques.

works.reason: 200g oats soaked in 300ml milk, 200g yoghurt and orange juice gives a good bircher for four, and two Bramleys stewed with honey make an ample tart topping.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers zesting, stirring, preparing two apples and toasting nuts, and the 480 minutes reflects the unattended overnight soak.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon appear in the steps, nothing unlisted is used apart from water, and 'sultanas' matches the raisins-or-sultanas id.

seasonal_feel.reason: Stored Bramleys are right for late March, and the stewed apple is the main flavour of the bowl rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, yoghurt, fruit and nuts make a filling, wholesome breakfast with only modest added honey.
